title: 1967 AHSME Problem 2
statement:
An equivalent of the expression

\[ \begin{aligned} &\left(\frac{x^2+1}{x}\right) \left(\frac{y^2+1}{y}\right)\\ &\quad+ \left(\frac{x^2-1}{y}\right) \left(\frac{y^2-1}{x}\right),\\ &\qquad xy\ne0, \end{aligned} \]

is:

solutions.text:
The first product is \[ xy+\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{x}+\frac1{xy}, \] while the second is \[ xy-\frac{x}{y}-\frac{y}{x}+\frac1{xy}. \] Adding gives \(2xy+\frac{2}{xy}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Expand each product into four terms
Look for cancellation of the \(\frac{x}{y}\) and \(\frac{y}{x}\) terms
